---
title: "Continuous uncorrelated models"
---

Use this page for Gaussian, Gamma, and inverse Gaussian examples. The teaching pattern is:

1. Fit the model.
2. Generate quantile residuals.
3. Draw `qnorm`.
4. Check residuals against fitted values and important covariates.

```stata
clear
set obs 120
set seed 20260510
generate double x = rnormal()
generate double y = exp(1 + .3*x + rnormal()/4)
glm y x, family(gamma) link(log)
qresid rq_gamma, family(gamma)
qnorm rq_gamma
predict double mu_gamma, mu
scatter rq_gamma mu_gamma, yline(0)
```

Gamma and inverse Gaussian examples should emphasize positive support. Gaussian examples should explain why the quantile residual coincides with a normal CDF residual under the fitted normal model, not with every regression residual diagnostic.
